papers.title_en: OPERA: A Unified Omnimodal Progressive Spatio-Temporal Reasoning Agent for Referring Video Segmentation
papers.authors: Jingchen Ni, Yuji Wang, Shannan Yan, Haoru Li, Sitong Chen, Chun Yuan
papers.evidence: 指代视频分割中的语言与掩码区域对齐
papers.tldr: 指代视频分割需处理文本、音频、参考图等异构多模态查询，要求跨模态理解与精确时空推理。OPERA基于单一MLLM构建统一智能体：时间轴上由粗到细筛选关键帧，空间轴上蒸馏跨模态语义并用GRPO增强定位，再密集传播掩码。在OmniAVS与Ref-AVS刷新SOTA，并零样本迁移到标准基准。它实现了统一的全模态渐进式时空推理。
papers.abstract_en: Referring video segmentation with heterogeneous multimodal queries---spanning text, audio, and reference images---demands both robust cross-modal understanding and precise spatio-temporal reasoning. We propose OPERA (Omnimodal Progressive spatio-tEmporal Reasoning Agent), a unified reasoning agent built on a single MLLM that performs dual-axis progressive reasoning via three specialized stages. Along the temporal axis, a Temporal Reasoning Agent narrows the frame search space through coarse-to-fine filtering to identify the most informative key frame. Along the spatial axis, a Distillation Agent establishes what to locate via cross-modal semantic distillation, and a Grounding Agent enhanced with GRPO determines where the target appears, with dense mask propagation completing the pixel-level output. OPERA sets a new state of the art on OmniAVS and Ref-AVS and transfers zero-shot to standard referring video segmentation benchmarks.

papers.title_en: Geometric Encoding for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Antonio Jun, Haoshui Yu, Zhengyi Lu, Huirong Fu, Yao Qiang
papers.evidence: 将二维感知与深度提升为三维空间编码供视觉语言模型推理
papers.tldr: 视觉语言模型能识别视频内容，却难以推理度量距离、物体尺寸和跨帧身份等空间时间属性。作者提出 Geometric Code，用感知层从单目 RGB 视频分割分类物体并恢复深度、相机位姿与内参，再由确定性几何引擎反投影、合并和清理，生成含位置、尺寸、数量、距离、出现顺序和房间几何的空间代码。该代码序列化进提示词，可伴随或替代视频，且无需训练或微调。在 VSI-Bench 上，2B/4B 开源模型平均准确率提升 4.1 点，绝对距离等数值估计任务提升 24.1 点。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are far more reliable at recognizing what appears in a video than at reasoning about its spatial and temporal properties, such as metric distances, object dimensions, and consistent object identities across frames. We present Geometric Code, a perception-to-geometry pipeline that computes explicit spatial structure from video and supplies it to VLMs as context to augment reasoning. A perception layer segments and classifies objects and recovers depth, camera pose, and intrinsics from monocular RGB video. A deterministic geometric engine then back-projects, merges, and cleans these outputs into a spatial code, including per-object positions, dimensions, counts, inter-object distances, appearance order, and room geometry. The code is serialized into VLMs' prompts, either alongside the video or replacing it entirely. Specifically, there is no component trained or fine-tuned in our approach. On VSI-Bench, augmenting 2B and 4B open models with the spatial code improves average accuracy by +4.1 points over the frames-only baseline, with the largest gains on numeric estimation tasks such as absolute distance (+24.1 points). The results suggest that explicitly computed geometry, delivered through the language channel, recovers spatial competence that small VLMs cannot extract from pixels alone.

papers.title_en: RRG-SLAM: Real-time Reflection-aware Gaussian SLAM for Indoor Scenes
papers.authors: Yong Liu, Keyang Ye, Zhexi Peng, Ruixian Mei, Kun Zhou, Tianjia Shao
papers.evidence: 带反射掩码与深度剔除的反射感知高斯SLAM
papers.tldr: 室内场景中镜面反射会干扰SLAM的跟踪与重建，导致几何与光度一致性被破坏。RRG-SLAM提出反射感知的TSDF-Gaussian混合表示，将漫反射外观与平面反射分量显式分离，是首个面向室内场景的实时反射感知高斯SLAM系统。系统先进行反射感知跟踪，再检测反射平面，并通过三阶段渲染生成基图像与反射图像，同时在线初始化、优化和剪枝高斯基元。实验表明其在重建质量、跟踪鲁棒性和新视角渲染上优于现有方法，且保持实时性。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce the first real-time reflection-aware Gaussian SLAM system for indoor scenes. The system features a reflection-aware TSDF-Gaussian hybrid representation that explicitly separates diffuse scene appearance from reflection components. The base scene is modeled by a TSDF volume and a set of base Gaussians capturing geometry and diffuse appearance, while planar reflections are represented by reflection Gaussian groups associated with detected reflective planes. The rendering is performed in three passes: TSDF raycasting first yields surface color, depth, plane IDs and reflection masks; base Gaussians are then rendered order-independently with depth culling and combined with the TSDF output to form the base image; finally, under the guidance of the plane ID map, reflection Gaussians from different reflection groups are rasterized only into their corresponding planar regions to generate the reflection image, which is subsequently composited with the base image via the reflection mask to produce the final output. For online reconstruction, our system first estimates the camera pose through reflection-aware tracking to suppress interference of reflection-dominated regions. It then identifies reflective planes using geometric, semantic, and temporal cues, and fuses the observations into the augmented TSDF volume with reflection-aware attributes. Afterwards the base and reflection Gaussians are initialized, optimized, and pruned online to maintain both reconstruction quality and efficiency. Experiments on a variety of datasets show that our method outperforms existing SLAM systems in reconstruction quality, tracking robustness, and novel-view rendering for indoor environments with reflections, while preserving real-time performance.
